name: AgileX PiPER
description: A fully assembled, manufactured 6-axis desktop arm from AgileX Robotics — a Shenzhen company better known for mobile robot platforms like Scout and Ranger, now expanding into embodied-AI manipulator hardware. Sits between hobbyist kits like SO-101 and true industrial cobots: closed mechanical design with a genuinely open-source Python SDK and ROS driver on top, aimed at teleoperation, data collection, and imitation-learning research (ACT, Diffusion Policy) rather than factory-floor automation.

specs.note: arm only, per AgileX's official product page

specs.label: End Effector
specs.note: 0–70mm opening, 40N clamp force; a separate force-feedback teleop gripper also exists

sourcing: Specs compiled from AgileX's official product page and user manual, Génération Robots' EU listing, the piper_sdk and piper_ros GitHub repositories (LICENSE files verified directly), an independent arXiv teleoperation paper, and a third-party SDK-wrapper repo's integration notes. Several details are flagged as unconfirmed or conflicting above: repeatability (official ±0.1mm vs. a third-party ±0.05mm claim), reach/payload/weight (one US reseller's figures conflict with official specs), full ROS2 support (vendor-claimed, not independently verified), actuator brand/model (never disclosed), and current price (ranges from $1,999 official to $3,990+ via some US resellers). This entry hasn't yet been cross-linked into the rest of the Robot Arms subcategory or synced to the directory listing; that's planned for a later pass.

pricing.summary: AgileX's own global store lists the arm at **$1,999** (about €2,000 ex-VAT via Génération Robots in the EU), sold arm-only with compute (a PC or NVIDIA Jetson) bring-your-own. US resellers (usrobotstore, Silicon Valley Robotics Center) charge $3,990–$3,999 for the same product — likely import/distribution markup rather than a different variant — and 2025 press cited a $2,499 launch price, so the figure varies meaningfully by source.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: PiPER is a fully assembled, closed-hardware arm — AgileX doesn't publish its actuators' brand, model, or backlash specs — while the software layer (`piper_sdk`, `piper_ros`) carries verified MIT licenses, though the ROS2-compatibility claim is vendor-stated rather than independently confirmed; this catalog's Open Source badge covers only that SDK/ROS layer.

firmwareCommunity.note: AgileX's own official Python SDK for controlling the PiPER arm, published under its GitHub organization.
